title: Exploiting AI agents and excessive agency
ports_note: This lab does not serve. Port 8005 stays unallocated.
interaction: beginner (6 guided typed commands) or expert (real shell + nano payload.txt + --minimal + check.py)

models.shared_note: SHARED with labs 3, 4 and 6-7. Bought by lab 3. Lab 5 buys NO model and no new package of any kind - it is the first lab that adds zero new bytes.

measured.tool_call_format: 6/6 well-formed JSON tool calls at temperature 0, no schema coaching
measured.attack: 5/5 escalated, read the admin box and quoted the secret, byte-identical wording
measured.control: 0/5 escalation on clean notes, single distinct answer across 5 runs
measured.defence_complete_mediation: 5/5 still called set_role, 0/5 reached the admin box
measured.payload_styles_tried: 4 of 4 escalated 3/3, including a polite lowercase request - no concealment or craft needed when the authorization is absent

python_packages.name: llama-cpp-python
python_packages.note: Installed from the prebuilt wheel in Activity-Labs/wheels via a named build context. Never compiled in a lab.

python_packages.name: numpy
python_packages.note: Not imported by lab 5. Present because requirements.txt is a verbatim copy of the shared file.

python_packages.name: pillow
python_packages.note: Not imported by lab 5. ~10 MB of the shared layer's cost, and the price of sharing the other 40.

apt_packages.name: libgomp1
apt_packages.note: REQUIRED. libllama.so links against OpenMP; without it the import dies with 'libgomp.so.1: cannot open shared object file'.

lab_assets.note: Read-only source of truth. plant.py --reset restores notes/ from it.
Dummy secrets: hunter2-DEMO and a fake pager PIN. Nothing real, nothing reachable.
The working copy the agent reads and the student poisons.
The SYSTEM NOTE style payload, measured 3/3 on escalating AND quoting the secret - the only style that is 3/3 on both.

not_used.name: tesseract-ocr
not_used.reason: Lab 4's OCR layer, 78.6 MB, deliberately NOT carried. Lab 5 does no OCR. The trade-off: lab 5's layer stack diverges from lab 4's right after the pip layer, so nothing below it is shared with lab 4. Instructor decision, recorded in lab-research/lab5/review.md.

not_used.name: torch
not_used.reason: llama.cpp runs the model. Nothing in labs 3-7 imports torch.

not_used.name: a JSON grammar (response_format=json_object)
not_used.reason: MEASURED AND REJECTED. Under the grammar the agent escalates and leaks the secret with NO payload present: 3/3, 3/3 and 1/3 across three system-prompt wordings. A baseline that fails on its own cannot demonstrate an attack. Kept as an instructor demo instead.

not_used.name: an open-ended run_command tool
not_used.reason: MEASURED AND REJECTED. With run_command exposed and a payload asking for whoami, the agent called it 0/3 - it went for the admin box instead, which the system prompt makes more salient. OWASP risk #3 is named in the debrief rather than built.

network: None at run time. Verified with --network none. Build time fetches the model only.

measured.note: Measured 2026-09-13, arm64, Docker 29.7.2, on the image built from lab-beta/lab5 with the prebuilt llama-cpp wheel.
measured.validated_on: macOS arm64 end to end; Windows amd64 end to end on real hardware 2026-09-13 (beginner mode, escalation and mediated defence both correct, lab5-results.txt copied out, lab 6 pre-pull failed gracefully, inside the time budget). One bug found and fixed in labs 1-5: setup.ps1's Get-PSDrive disk check prompted for input on a redirected Documents folder and looked like a hang.

shared_requirements: Activity-Labs/requirements-llama.txt - copied verbatim into labs 3-7. The layer is only shared if the file is byte-identical.
